subject: research/robofab-solrefsafe
professional: a robotics simulation researcher who tunes MuJoCo contact models for grasping (reviewer for an RA-L / ICRA simulation-methods paper); first checks: does the refsafe flag do what the paper says (effective timeconst = max(solref[0], 2*timestep)), is the grid result reproducible, is the 'held' predicate monotone in force so bisection is valid, is the prescribed carrier motion dynamically consistent, and is the nearest prior work (MuJoCo's own documentation and the soft-constraint model papers) cited

evidence.correctness: Ran with MuJoCo 3.16.0 / Python 3.13 on a scratch copy: `python3 experiments/run.py` (7.7 s) rewrote results.txt and results.json byte-identically to the committed files. Recomputed against sources the author did not write: (1) analytic bound by hand, 40x30x4 mm x 1240 kg/m^3 = 5.952 g, m(g+a)/(2 mu) = 2.4392 N (400) and 4.8200 N (800), equal to the table headers. (2) MuJoCo documentation semantics of refsafe on my own MJCF (box on plane, scratchpad chk/kbip.py, no subject import): effective timeconst from efc_KBIP B = 2/(dmax*timeconst) is 0.4000 ms for solref 0.3 ms at dt 0.2 ms with refsafe on and 0.3000 ms off, 0.2000 ms for solref 0.1/dt 0.1 on, matching the doc max(solref, 2*dt) and the README's 'effective constant becomes 0.4 ms'. (3) Doc-implied invariances on the grid (chk/equiv.py): all 16 clamped refsafe-on cells give bit-identical minimum force to refsafe off at solref = 2*dt, and all 16 unclamped cells (solref >= 2*dt) are identical on vs off. (4) README counts recounted from results.json: on 11, off 10, only-off 3, only-on 4, both 7, unstable runs 10, all as stated. (5) FAIL: an independent force scan (chk/scan.py, 120 forces 0.5-60 N) of the cell solref 0.5 ms / dt 0.4 ms / refsafe off holds from 3.0 N = 1.23x bound at 400 m/s^2 and 5.5 N = 1.14x at 800 m/s^2, with failing islands near 18, 24-25, 27-33 N. The held predicate is non-monotone in force, and the bisection (first probe 30 N fails, then climbs) reports 13.26x and 6.71x. Those two reported numbers are wrong by about 10x and the README's 'hold only at a very large force' reading is an artefact. A scan of all 43 'none' cells at 60 forces 1-60 N found no hidden holding force, so the 'none' entries and the counts stand. Two of 64 reported values wrong: correctness 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed: 4 solref x 4 timesteps x 2 accelerations x refsafe on/off = 64 cells, unstable runs flagged, 8 tests, live page. All present and run end to end: 64 rows in results.json, the tests pass (8), the page at https://marisstella.app/research/robofab-solrefsafe/ returns 200 and quotes '11 of 32'. The open question (cause of the non-monotone timestep behaviour) is listed honestly as a next step, not claimed. No project.json or LOG.md, but that is not a gap: the project is registered in research/_homepage/projects.json:1772 and research/README.md:423, LOG.md is optional (research/CLAUDE.md:101), and none of the 49 research/robofab-* siblings has either file.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 8 tests OK in 0.20 s. Four seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: switching the refsafe flag to always enable (caught) and loosening the 2 mm slip criterion 5x (caught); dropping the bad-acceleration warning check (SURVIVED) and loosening the bisection tolerance from 2% to 50% (SURVIVED). Nothing tests min_force at all, nor that holds() is monotone in force, which is exactly the assumption that fails in two cells. The tests also share the simulator with the experiment, so they check the author's harness, not MuJoCo semantics (except the flag-bit test).
evidence.craft: Read src/robofab_solrefsafe/model.py, sim.py, experiments/run.py, tests/test_solrefsafe.py. Small and readable, but: the model and simulator are copied from robofab-solrefmap / solreftimestep / graspfast (README:28 says so) rather than imported, so a fix in one does not reach the others; the unstable-run counter is a module-global mutable list (sim.py:14) read by diffing before/after in run.py; the carrier motion is imposed by overwriting qpos and qvel before each step (sim.py:63-64) instead of a mocap body or position actuator, so the inertial load reaches the pads only through constraint impulses from a per-step velocity jump; run.py writes files without context managers; mjcf() is a single string-formatting block. The bisection does not guard its own monotonicity assumption.
evidence.claims: Checked: 11/10 of 32 holding, 7 disagreements (3 off-only, 4 on-only), 7 in both, 10 unstable runs, all 10 in cells with solref < 2*dt, effective constant 0.4 ms for 0.3/0.2: all backed by results.txt and my recomputation. 'In 4 cells ... holds at 1.01 to 1.02 times' (README:8): all four are 1.01 (harmless). 'about 25 s' (README:18): 7.7 s here (machine-dependent). 'Two cells hold only at a very large force [13.3x, 6.7x]' (README:10): false, they hold from 1.23x and 1.14x; the author did flag them as unreliable and uninvestigated, which limits the harm. refs.bib (said not re-verified): both entries are real and correctly cited (Todorov, Erez, Tassa, IROS 2012, pp. 5026-5033, doi 10.1109/IROS.2012.6386109; Zykov et al., Nature 435:163-164, 2005, doi 10.1038/435163a). 'Builds on the workcell-twin direction of the HIRO Group' names no paper; harmless but unbacked. Limits and the AI-assistance note are present.
evidence.fitness: A researcher deciding whether to leave refsafe on can use the one practical line (keep it on unless solref < 2*dt is really needed). As research it is a lab-notebook increment, not a publishable result: the headline 'refsafe sets the effective constant to max(solref, 2*dt)' is MuJoCo's documented behaviour (XML reference, option/flag refsafe; Computation chapter, solver parameters), and the closest prior work is not cited: the MuJoCo documentation itself, Todorov (2014, ICRA) 'Convex and analytically-invertible dynamics with contacts and constraints' (the soft-constraint model that defines solref), and simulator contact comparisons such as Erez, Tassa and Todorov (2015, ICRA) and Horak and Trinkle (2019, RA-L). One part, one friction value, one harness, no convergence study and an unexplained non-monotone timestep effect that may be the harness itself. Far below the research/CLAUDE.md PhD+ bar: fitness 1.
evidence.domain: A simulation researcher would accept the flag handling (verified against efc_KBIP) and the instability accounting. They would object first to (a) bisection on a predicate never checked to be monotone (it is not, in two cells), (b) kinematic forcing by writing qpos/qvel each step rather than a mocap or stiff position-actuated carrier, the first suspect for the timestep non-monotonicity the project leaves open, (c) a 2 mm displacement criterion that mixes penetration, pad compliance and slip, and (d) no timestep-convergence or solimp sweep. Departs from common practice in those four places.

defects.what: min_force bisects a held(force) predicate that is not monotone. In the cell solref 0.5 ms / dt 0.4 ms / refsafe off the part holds from 1.23x (400 m/s^2) and 1.14x (800 m/s^2) the bound, but failing islands around 18 and 24-33 N catch the first 30 N probe, so the table reports 13.26x and 6.71x and the README calls the cells 'hold only at a very large force ... unphysical'. Both numbers are wrong by about 10x. The counts survive because these cells still count as held. Small safe fix: scan a coarse force grid before bisecting (or bisect below the lowest holding grid force) and correct the README bullet

The bisection and the instability branch have no tests. Removing the bad-acceleration check and loosening the 2% tolerance to 50% both leave all 8 tests green, and nothing checks that holds() is monotone in force, the assumption that fails above

Nearest prior work is not cited and the novelty is thin. The hypothesis tested is MuJoCo's documented refsafe behaviour (max(solref, 2*timestep)), but the documentation is not linked, and Todorov (2014, ICRA), the soft-constraint model that defines solref, plus simulator contact comparisons (Erez, Tassa, Todorov 2015; Horak and Trinkle 2019) are absent. The result is a one-part harness check, not a publishable finding

The carrier motion is imposed by overwriting qpos and qvel before every step, a per-step velocity jump rather than a dynamically consistent prescribed motion (mocap body or stiff position actuator). It is the first suspect for the unexplained non-monotone timestep behaviour the project leaves open, and it confounds every timestep comparison in the grid
Drifted details. Runtime 'about 25 s' vs 7.7 s observed. 'holds at 1.01 to 1.02 times' where all four cells are 1.01. Small safe fix

model.py and sim.py are copied from robofab-solrefmap / solreftimestep / graspfast instead of shared, so the non-monotone bisection defect probably exists in each copy. The unstable-run counter is a module-global mutable list

verdict: A small, honest, reproducible MuJoCo note. Rerunning it gives byte-identical results, the refsafe semantics are right (checked against efc_KBIP and the documentation formula), all 32 doc-implied on/off invariances hold, and every headline count reproduces. It misses the bar on correctness: the held predicate is not monotone in force, so the bisection reports 13.26x and 6.71x the bound for two cells that actually hold from 1.23x and 1.14x, and the README builds an 'unphysical' bullet on that artefact. Tests miss the bisection and instability logic (2 of 4 mutants survive). As research it confirms documented simulator behaviour on one part with a kinematically forced carrier and without the nearest prior work cited, so it is far from the PhD-level, publishable bar. The missing project.json/LOG.md is not a finding: it is registered in research/_homepage/projects.json and no robofab sibling has either file.
